subject: MAP: POC network onramp — API keys, org invite, IP allowlist, VPC peering
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@catalyx.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@catalyx.ai
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC MAP kickoff: env access & network asks

Hi Rishi —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We reviewed internally and we’re ready to start the POC MAP. High-level asks so we can lock the calendar and start provisioning: 

- Org invite: please add a Catalyx service account and one user (elena.morales@catalyx.ai) to our trial org.
- API keys: we need a pair of non-prod keys and guidance on rotation / TTL for ephemeral tokens.
- IP allowlist: we operate behind a managed firewall. Can you confirm the list of Redwood egress IPs (or ranges) we need to allow?
- VPC peering: we run in AWS us-west-2; request a short checklist (IAM roles, routing steps, expected maintenance window).

Target timeline: we’d like the onboarding runway to start May 31 and be able to run initial ingest and latency tests by June 3. If that’s tight on your side, propose alternatives.

Attached is our initial MAP doc and a short procurement checklist (procurement@catalyx.ai is cc’d).

Appreciate a single owner for each item so we can track.

Best,
Elena
Elena Morales
Head of Platforms, Catalyx.ai

Thanks Elena — solid list. I’ll be lead for the MAP on the Redwood side and will coordinate owners internally. Quick responses / actions from our side: 

1) Org invite + API keys
- We can create an org-level trial and invite elena.morales@catalyx.ai today.
- For API access, we provide scoped API keys and we also support short-lived ephemeral tokens via our CLI. Recommend starting with scoped keys (non-prod) and switching to ephemeral for production load tests.

2) IP allowlist
- Can you share the IP ranges your firewall team controls for egress? We will provide the specific Redwood egress CIDRs for us-west-2 within 24 hours.

3) VPC peering (us-west-2)
- Jordan (cc’d) will own the peering checklist and route table guidance. We typically do: exchange AWS account IDs + VPC IDs -> create peering -> update route tables -> test. Peering maintenance is low-risk but we can schedule a 30-min window.

Proposed owners:
- Redwood MAP owner: rishi_malhotra
- Tech lead (peering + routes): jordan_blake
- Security & compliance checklist: neha_kapoor

I’m attaching a short SOW draft for review. Next steps: can we lock a 30-min kickoff on Tue or Wed? I’ll also send the org invite once we confirm the primary admin email.

Thanks,
Rishi

Looping in a few details from security/ops POV.

Elena — welcome. A couple of practical points so we can avoid rework: 
- For the org invite, please confirm the admin email (is elena.morales@catalyx.ai the person who will accept invites or do you prefer a shared admin alias?).
- For API keys, do you need per-team keys or a single pipeline key for the POC? Per-team is slightly more operational overhead but gives clearer audit trails.
- IP allowlist: if you can share your managed firewall egress IP block(s) I’ll compare with our egress pool and flag any overlaps.

Jordan — can you draft the peering playbook (1–page) that includes: required IAM role assertions, required subnets (we recommend a /27 for test peering endpoints), test steps, and rollback instructions. If possible, include the NAT/eBPF note for customers who use NAT gateways.

I’ll coordinate security questionnaire items (SOC2 scoping) — Elena, we can fast-track the initial answers for the POC to avoid procurement bottlenecks.

Neha
Neha Kapoor
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: Elena Morales <elena.morales@catalyx.ai>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 11:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC MAP kickoff: env access & network asks

On Wed, May 25, 2027 at 08:27 AM neha_kapoor@redwood.ai wrote:
> Jordan — can you draft the peering playbook (1–page) that includes: required IAM role assertions, required subnets (we recommend a /27 for test peering endpoints), test steps, and rollback instructions. If possible, include the NAT/eBPF note for customers who use NAT gateways.

I’ve pulled together the short technical checklist below (happy to drop into a one-pager doc):

- Exchange: AWS account IDs and VPC IDs (Catalyx to provide).
- CIDR: we prefer non-overlapping /24s; for the peering endpoints we request a /27 per environment. If you have existing overlap, we can use proxy routing but it adds complexity.
- IAM: create a cross-account role with these managed policies: AmazonVPCFullAccess (for peering setup) + logs:PutLogEvents for basic diagnostics.
- Routing: after peering is accepted, add routes in both route tables for the counterpart CIDR.
- DNS resolution: enable "allow DNS resolution from peer" if you need private-hostname lookups.
- Validation: simple ping/tcp check from a bastion + verify route tables.
- Expected timeline: 2–4 hours of work with both teams synchronized; schedule a 30–60 minute window for acceptance testing.

IP allowlist: Redwood egress ranges for us-west-2 (non-exhaustive sample) — 54.214.128.0/18, 34.210.0.0/16. I’ll confirm the canonical set after we open the ticket.

API keys: we’ll create scoped keys with the ability to restrict by route and token TTL. For the POC I recommend: 30d TTL scoped key + create a short-lived ephemeral token for any automated stress tests.

Action items assigned: 
- Catalyx: provide VPC ID(s) + preferred admin email + firewall egress blocks (Elena)
- Redwood (Stephanie): publish canonical egress CIDRs + produce peering playbook draft (Jordan to review)
- Redwood (Rishi): send org invite once Catalyx confirms admin email

I’m available Tue/Wed for a 30-minute window 9–12 PT.

—
Stephanie Nguyen
Cloud Network Engineer, Redwood Inference
